 Bbsr and Another
Coram:

THE HON'BLE MR.JUSTICE BIRAJA PRASANNA SATAPATHY  ORDER 28.10.2025 Order No.
04.
1. This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.
2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the parties.
3. The present Writ Petition has been filed inter alia with the following prayer:

The Petitioner, therefore, prays that your lordships would graciously be pleased to admit this petition and call for the records, and after hearing the parties, be pleased to quash the Petitioner's disqualification/rejection in OSSC FSO Recruitment, vide Advt. Dated 23.12.2019 & 30.12.2020, and be pleased to direct the Ops - OSSC to treat the petitioner as eligible on the strength of M.Sc. Biotechnology and appoint him as Food Safety Officer with notional seniority and consequential service benefits as per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in Chandra Shekhar Singh & Others v.
State of Jharkhand reported in AIR 2025 SC 1733;
Or, in the alternative, direct creation of a supernumerary post for him, as per Chandra Shekhar Singh (Supreme Court).

And for this act of kindness, the petitioner, as in duty bound, shall forever pray.

4. It is contended that prayer so made by the present petitioner is covered by a decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in AIR 2025 Supreme Court, 1733 (Chandra Shekhar Singh and Others Vs. State of Jharkhand and Others).
5.

entities.text: AIR 2025 Supreme Court, 1733 (Chandra Shekhar Singh and Others Vs. State of Jharkhand and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Addl. Govt. Advocate on the other hand contended that if as contended, claim of the Petitioner is covered by the aforesaid decision, let the Petitioner move the Commission for consideration of his grievance.

6. Having heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and considering the submission made,
this Court while disposing the Writ Petition permits the Petitioner to move Opp. Party No.1 for consideration of his grievance as made in the Writ Petition.

7. It is observed that if such an application will be filed before Opp. Party No. 1 within a period of 2 (two) weeks hence, Opp. Party No.1 shall do well to take a lawful decision on the same within a period of three (3) months from the date of receipt of such representation.
The order so passed by Opp. Party No. 1 be communicated to the Petitioner.

8. It is further observed that while taking such a decision, relevancy and effect of the judgment relied on by the learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner be taken into consideration, if it is applicable to the Petitioner's claim.
9.
Petitioner is directed to provide a copy of this order along with the decision in the case of Chandra Shekhar Singh as cited supra before Opp. Party No.1 for compliance.
10.The Writ Petition accordingly stands disposed of.
(Biraja Prasanna Satapathy) Judge sangita
